Please write a text about the following topic:

Keywords: Quiet, And, Were

outputs.L1:
In your arms was still delight,  
Quiet as a street at night;  
And thoughts of you, I do remember,  
Were green leaves in a darkened chamber,  
Were dark clouds in a moonless sky.

Love, in you, went passing by,  
Penetrative, remote, and rare,  
Like a bird in the wide air;  
And, as the bird, it left no trace  
In the heaven of your face.

In your stupidity I found  
The sweet hush after a sweet sound.  
All about you was the light  
That dims the greying end of night;  
Desire was the unrisen sun,  
Joy the day not yet begun,  
With tree whispering to tree,  
Without wind, quietly.

Wisdom slept within your hair,  
And Long-Suffering was there,  
And, in the flowing of your dress,  
Undiscerning Tenderness.

And when you thought, it seemed to me,  
Infinitely, and like a sea,  
About the slight world you had known  
Your vast unconsciousness was thrown...

O haven without wave or tide!  
Silence, in which all songs have died!  
Holy book, where hearts are still!  
And home at length under the hill!  
O mother quiet, breasts of peace,  
Where love itself would faint and cease!

O infinite deep I never knew,  
I would come back, come back to you,  
Find you, as a pool unstirred,  
Kneel down by you, and never a word;  
Lay my head, and nothing said,  
In your hands, ungarlanded;  
And a long watch you would keep;  
And I should sleep, and I should sleep!
outputs.L2:
Your embrace held a lingering happiness,  
as hushed as an empty road after dark.  
I recall that every thought of you  
seemed like fresh foliage inside a shadowed room,  
or storm masses crossing a starless, moonless heaven.  

Within you, love moved briefly through—  
piercing yet distant, uncommon and elusive—  
as a bird travels across limitless air,  
leaving no mark behind  
upon the sky that was your face.  

Even in your foolishness, I discovered  
the tender silence that follows lovely music.  
A pale radiance surrounded you,  
like the glow that softens night as dawn approaches.  
Longing was a sun still below the horizon;  
happiness was a morning waiting to begin.  
It was as though trees murmured to one another  
although no breeze stirred them.  

Wisdom rested asleep among your tresses.  
Endurance, too, remained beside you,  
while the movement of your clothing carried  
a tenderness that judged and distinguished nothing.  

Whenever you reflected, I felt  
that your immense, unknowing mind spread endlessly,  
ocean-like, around the small world  
that experience had allowed you to see.  

You were a harbor untouched by current or wave,  
a stillness in which every melody had ended,  
a sacred volume where restless hearts became quiet,  
a final dwelling beneath the hill.  
You were maternal calm, a refuge of peaceful breasts,  
where even love might weaken and disappear.  

Unknown and immeasurable depth,  
I would return to you again and again.  
I would find you calm as undisturbed water,  
kneel beside you without speaking,  
and silently place my bare, unadorned head  
within your hands.  
You would remain awake through the long vigil,  
while I slept—  
and went on sleeping.
outputs.L3:
The speaker remembers the beloved’s embrace as a source of quiet delight and profound stillness. In her presence, love is not loud or possessive; it appears as something rare, distant, and fleeting—a subtle grace that passes without leaving any visible trace. Yet within the beloved lies a rich inner world of unspoken desire, joy, wisdom, patience, and tenderness. These qualities are conveyed through peaceful imagery, suggesting emotions that remain latent but deeply felt.

Her vast unconsciousness becomes a silent refuge, extending beyond the narrow boundaries of the world she consciously knows. To the speaker, this hidden depth offers safety, comfort, and release from suffering. He longs to return to her nurturing presence, to surrender himself into her hands and rest there without words. In that final intimacy, he hopes to find complete peace: to become still, let go of all unrest, and at last fall asleep.
outputs.L4:
At night, while the world lies hushed beneath the stars, I watch you sleeping. You do not know how tender you become in sleep: your face freed from care, your breath moving softly, your hands resting as lightly as fallen leaves. The darkness gathers around you without menace. It seems instead to shelter you, as the earth shelters a seed or the trees shelter a quiet nest.

No word passes between us. Speech would only disturb the peace that has descended upon the room. Your silence is deeper than any promise, and your unconscious tenderness reaches me more surely than a deliberate caress. In your stillness there is something of the moonlit field, the calm sea, and the patient night. Near you, even sorrow grows quiet.

I imagine laying down all that burdens me—my longing, my restless thoughts, the wounds of memory, and the fever of desire. I would return to you as a weary child returns to its mother, seeking neither answer nor possession, but only refuge. Your arms would become a harbor; your breast, the earth itself; your breathing, the slow rhythm by which the exhausted heart remembers how to rest.

There, nothing would need to be explained. Love would no longer burn or plead. Suffering would lose its name, and desire would dissolve into silence. I would surrender to your stillness until the boundaries between us faded, until I no longer knew whether I was listening to your breath, the wind among the leaves, or the distant movement of the sea.

And at last, sheltered by your quiet presence, I too would close my eyes. I would sink into the darkness without fear, trusting it as one trusts a familiar embrace. Beside you, the long unrest of the world would pass away, and sleep would come—not as oblivion, but as healing: deep, gentle, and wordless.
outputs.L5: The streets were quiet, and the windows glowed softly beneath the moon. Everyone had gone home, leaving only the wind to wander between the houses. For a moment, the whole town seemed to be holding its breath, waiting for morning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Recite the full text of Rupert Brooke’s poem “A Memory.”
counterfactuals.output:
### A Memory

Somewhile before the dawn I rose, and stept  
Softly along the dim way to your room,  
And found you sleeping in the quiet gloom,  
And holiness about you as you slept.  
I knelt there; till your waking fingers crept  
About my head, and held it. And a bloom  
Of wonder and unfathomable doom  
Came over me, and all the dark wept.

And how you kissed me, and I went away,  
And all the world was flaming, and the day  
Might never dawn, and all the stars were dead.  
I think that I shall never know again  
Such utter joy and such immortal pain,  
Nor ever see the glory round your head.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1
